Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p

Enum Class TrustDecision

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<TrustDecision>
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p.TrustDecision
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<TrustDecision>, Constable
public enum TrustDecision extends Enum<TrustDecision>
The pure verdict of a trust-on-first-use (TOFU) check: given the fingerprint we have pinned for a peer (if any) and the one it actually presented during the NoiseXXHandshake, decide whether to proceed, warn, or refuse. This type does no I/O and holds no state, so the trust logic is unit-testable in isolation and reusable by both apps; IdentityStore supplies the persisted pins.

The three outcomes mirror SSH's host-key model:

  • FIRST_CONTACT - we have never seen this peer, so there is nothing to compare against. TOFU says: proceed, and remember the fingerprint now so a future change is detectable.
  • MATCH - the presented fingerprint equals the pin. Proceed quietly.
  • MISMATCH - a pin exists and the presented fingerprint differs. This is the man-in-the-middle signal: the peer's identity changed since we pinned it. Refuse by default and require an explicit, loud user override (IdentityStore.overrideMismatch(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.lang.String)).

A missing or blank presented fingerprint is always MISMATCH: an unauthenticated peer is never trusted, first contact or not.
